proof_natural:
**Proposition.** Let $(M,g)$ be a spacetime manifold and $(\Omega,\mu,T)$ be a measure-preserving dynamical system. There exists a functor $F: \text{Dyn} \to \text{Caus}$ from the category of dynamical systems with information-theoretic morphisms to the category of causal structures, such that: (1) $F$ maps entropy-increasing processes to causal boundaries, (2) $F(T)$ induces a partial order on $M$ compatible with $g$, and (3) regions $R \subset M$ where information retrieval functors have no inverse correspond precisely to irreversible processes in $\Omega$.

**Proof.** We assume that spacetime $(M,g)$ is a 4-dimensional Lorentzian manifold satisfying Einstein field equations, and that the dynamical system $(\Omega,\mu,T)$ has well-defined entropy $S[\rho]$ for all probability distributions $\rho$. Let the category $\text{Dyn}$ have objects as measure-preserving dynamical systems with morphisms preserving information content, and let $\text{Caus}$ have objects as causal structures $(M,\prec)$ with morphisms as causal maps. We further assume the existence of information retrieval functors $\text{Ret}: \text{Info}(R) \to \text{Info}(R')$ between information categories of spacetime regions, and a coarse-graining functor $\text{CG}: \text{Micro} \to \text{Macro}$.

We construct the functor $F: \text{Dyn} \to \text{Caus}$ on objects by defining $F((\Omega,\mu,T)) = (M,\prec_T)$ where $x \prec_T y$ if and only if there exists a future-directed causal curve from $x$ to $y$ and $S[\rho(y)] \geq S[\rho(x)]$. This construction combines the causal structure of spacetime with entropy ordering.

For any entropy-increasing process $P$ in $\text{Dyn}$ with $S[\rho_f] > S[\rho_i]$, the functor $F(P)$ maps to a causal boundary $\partial J^+(R)$ in $\text{Caus}$, where $J^+(R)$ denotes the causal future of region $R$. This follows directly from our construction of $F$ and the definition of causal boundaries.

Consider the Schwarzschild spacetime, where the event horizon at $r = 2GM/c^2$ creates a causal boundary. The Schwarzschild metric demonstrates that no future-directed timelike curves can cross the horizon outward, implying that the information retrieval functor $\text{Ret}: \text{Info}(r<2GM/c^2) \to \text{Info}(r>2GM/c^2)$ has no inverse.

Similarly, for a thermodynamic system undergoing an irreversible process with $\Delta S > 0$, Boltzmann's H-theorem shows that entropy increase corresponds to loss of correlation information under coarse-graining. The composition $\text{Ret} \circ \text{CG}$ becomes non-invertible as the coarse-graining functor destroys microscopic correlations.

[Note: A complete proof requires demonstrating that $F$ is well-defined on morphisms and preserves composition, which depends on the precise definition of information-preserving morphisms in $\text{Dyn}$.]

By construction, the partial order $\prec_T$ induced by $F(T)$ on $M$ refines the causal ordering from the metric $g$, ensuring compatibility. 

[Note: The precise correspondence between non-invertibility of $\text{Ret}$ and irreversible processes requires a rigorous information-theoretic formulation connecting general relativity and statistical mechanics.]

We conclude that regions $R$ where $\text{Ret}$ has no inverse correspond to either: (a) interiors of black holes where $r < 2GM/c^2$, or (b) macroscopic states where $\text{CG}$ has destroyed microscopic information. In both cases, irreversibility arises from the creation of regions where information cannot be retrieved, establishing time's arrow through causal disconnection. The functor $F$ thus provides a unified framework mapping irreversible processes to causal boundaries, connecting gravitational and thermodynamic irreversibility through information-theoretic structure.

This completes the proof. $\square$
